heading.b: Non-complying electoral material—additional provisions regarding how-to-vote cards

block.txt: Without limiting section 180, electoral material consisting of or containing a how-to-vote card contravenes this Subdivision if the card does not comply with this section.

heading.b: Non-complying how-to-vote cards for registered parties

block.txt: A how-to-vote card containing voting directions as to how to vote for or in accordance with the recommendations of a registered party does not comply with this section if—
the party has nominated no candidate for the election, or
the voting directions give a preference to a candidate not nominated by it without first giving higher preferences to all candidates nominated by it.

A how-to-vote card containing voting directions as to how to vote for or in accordance with the recommendations of a group does not comply with this section if the voting directions give a preference to a candidate who is not a member of the group without first giving higher preferences to all candidates who are members of the group.

heading.b: Non-complying how-to-vote cards for individual candidates

block.txt: A how-to-vote card containing voting directions as to how to vote for or in accordance with the recommendations of a particular candidate does not comply with this section if—
whether or not the candidate is a member of a group—the voting directions do not contain a voting direction for the candidate to receive the first preference, or

where the candidate is a member of a group—the voting directions give a preference to a candidate who is not a member of the group without first giving higher preferences to all candidates who are members of the group.

heading.b: Non-complying how-to-vote cards using group voting squares—voting above and below the line

block.txt: A how-to-vote card containing voting directions as to how to vote for or in accordance with the recommendations of a group of candidates by using a group voting square does not comply with this section if the voting directions also give preferences (“below the line”) for—
only some of the individual members of the group, or
individual members of the group in a different order from that appearing in the list of candidates in the group on the ballot paper.

Subsection (5) ensures that in these circumstances the material must be internally consistent, since voting by using a group voting square implies voting for all the candidates in the group and in the order in which their names appear.

heading.b: Non-complying how-to-vote cards without group voting squares—no indication of requirement to vote for at least 15 candidates

block.txt: A how-to-vote card containing voting directions as to how to vote without using group voting squares and that do not give preferences for at least 15 candidates to be elected does not comply with this section if the voting directions do not contain a statement as to how many other preferences must be marked on the ballot paper.

heading.b: Electoral matter involving joint voting directions

block.txt: Despite sections 180 and 181, electoral material consisting of or containing a how-to-vote card does not contravene this Subdivision merely because the card contains matter described in this section.
The electoral material consists of or contains a how-to-vote card which contains the joint voting directions of 2 or more participants in respect of one or more electoral districts, so long as—
one or other of the participants has nominated a candidate for each one of the districts, and
the material does not direct or suggest that a candidate nominated by none of the participants should be given the first preference vote, and
the application for registration of the material was made jointly by the registered officer of the participant or candidate, as the case may be, and
the application for registration of the material otherwise complies with the relevant requirements of this Subdivision.

The electoral material contains directions or suggestions (express or implied) as to how to vote in accordance with the joint voting directions of 2 or more participants in respect of a periodic Council election, so long as—
each of the participants has nominated at least one candidate for the election, and
the material does not direct or suggest that a candidate or candidates nominated by none of the participants should be given the first or highest preference or preferences, and
the application for registration of the material was made jointly by the registered officer or the first candidate of the group of candidates, as the case may be, of each participant, and
the application for registration of the material otherwise complies with the relevant requirements of this Subdivision (apart from section 181 (2) and (3)).
In this section—
participant means a registered party or a group of candidates registered under the Electoral Funding Act 2018.

heading.b: Printing, publishing and distributing non-complying electoral material

block.txt: A person must not, during the regulated period, print, publish or distribute electoral material that contravenes Subdivision 2.
Maximum penalty—
for an individual—60 penalty units or imprisonment for 6 months, or both, or
otherwise—300 penalty units.
A person must not, during the regulated period, publicly display or permit or cause to be publicly displayed, a poster containing or consisting of electoral material that contravenes Subdivision 2.
Maximum penalty—
for an individual—60 penalty units or imprisonment for 6 months, or both, or
otherwise—300 penalty units.
A person must not, during the regulated period, display or permit or cause to be displayed a poster—
on or within any premises occupied or used by, or under the control or management of—
the Crown or a NSW Government agency, or
any council or county council, or
on or within any other premises, unless the person—
was the owner or a joint owner of the premises, or
performed the act concerned with the permission in writing of the owner or a joint owner of the premises.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of a corporation—12.5 penalty units, or
in any other case—2.5 penalty units.
Subsection (2) (a) does not apply in relation to a poster—
on the outer wall, fence or other boundary of the grounds of an enclosure in which a building used for voting is situated, or
within the grounds of an enclosure in which a building used for voting is situated, or
on a vehicle on a road or road related area (within the meaning of section 4 (1) of the Road Transport Act 2013), or
fixed or attached to a table or stall on a footpath or other public place at any time on the day of voting for an election.

The display of election posters also constitutes development for the purposes of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979. Subdivision 13 (Election signs) of Division 2 of Part 2 of State Environmental Planning Policy (Exempt and Complying Development Codes) 2008 provides that the display of election posters is exempt development, subject to conditions, during the period commencing 5 weeks before and ending 1 week after the election day concerned.

heading.b: Writing, drawing or depicting electoral matter

block.txt: A person must not, during the regulated period, write, draw or depict any electoral matter directly on any property, being a roadway, footpath, building, vehicle, vessel, hoarding or place (whether it is or is not a public place and whether on land or water).
Maximum penalty—
in the case of a corporation—15 penalty units, or
in any other case—3 penalty units.
A person is not guilty of an offence under this section if the person—
was the owner or joint owner of the property, or
performed the act concerned with the permission in writing of the owner or a joint owner of the property.
Without limiting subsection (2), a person is not guilty of an offence under this section involving a vehicle, vessel or hoarding if the person—
was the owner or joint owner of the premises on which the vehicle, vessel or hoarding was situated, or
performed the act concerned with the permission in writing of the owner or a joint owner of the premises.
Subsections (2) and (3) do not apply to any premises or property occupied or used by, or under the control or management of—
the Crown or a NSW Government agency, or
any council or county council.

heading.b: Name and address on electoral material

block.txt: A person must not, during the regulated period, print, publish, distribute or publicly display electoral material, other than the announcement in a newspaper of the holding of a meeting, without legibly showing on the material the name and address of an individual on whose instructions the material was printed, published, distributed or publicly displayed.
Maximum penalty—
for an individual—20 penalty units or imprisonment for 6 months, or both, or
otherwise—100 penalty units.

For electoral material that is a social media post, the name and address of the individual on whose instructions the material was published or distributed must be published or distributed in a way, if any, prescribed by the regulations.
For a 3-minute TikTok video, the regulations may prescribe that the name and address be displayed for a specified number of seconds or with a specified size as a percentage of the video display.
Subsection (1) does not apply in relation to—
a T-shirt, lapel button, lapel badge, pen, pencil or balloon, or
a business or visiting card that promotes the candidacy of any person in an election, or
a letter or other card—
that bears the name and address of the sender, and
that does not contain a representation or purported representation of a ballot paper for use in an election, or
any other article or thing prescribed (or of a class prescribed) by the regulations.

heading.b: Authorisation of advertisements on electronic billboards, digital road signs etc to be displayed

block.txt: A person must not, during the regulated period, display any electoral matter on an electronic billboard, digital road sign or other similar device, unless the matter contains, in visible, legible characters, the name and address of an individual on whose instructions the matter was displayed.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of a corporation—100 penalty units, or
in any other case—20 penalty units or imprisonment for 6 months, or both.

A person must not, during the regulated period, cause, permit or authorise an automated telephone call containing electoral matter to be made to another person, unless the call contains, in a clear voice, spoken in English, the name and address of an individual on whose instructions the call was made.
Maximum penalty—
for an individual—20 penalty units or imprisonment for 6 months, or both, or
otherwise—100 penalty units.

heading.b: Publication of paid electoral advertisements on the internet

block.txt: A person must not, during the regulated period, publish an advertisement containing electoral matter on the internet, or cause, permit or authorise such an advertisement to be published, if—
the advertisement is paid for by the person or another person, and
the name and address of an individual who authorised the advertisement do not appear within the advertisement.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of a corporation—100 penalty units, or
in any other case—20 penalty units or imprisonment for 6 months, or both.
A person does not commit the offence in subsection (1) if the person establishes that the matter published on the internet forms part of a general commentary on a website.

heading.b: Encouraging ticks or crosses on ballot papers

block.txt: A person must not, during the regulated period, print, publish, distribute or publicly display any electoral material that encourages any elector to place a tick or a cross in a square on a ballot paper.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of a corporation—100 penalty units, or
in any other case—20 penalty units or imprisonment for 6 months, or both.

heading.b: Certain digitally generated electoral material prohibited

block.txt: A person must not, during the regulated period, print, publish, distribute or publicly display digitally generated electoral material that contains a depiction of a simulated person performing an act that the real person depicted in the depiction did not perform.
Maximum penalty—
for an individual—60 penalty units or imprisonment for 6 months, or both, or
otherwise—300 penalty units.
It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence against this section if the defendant establishes that—

the printing, publication, distribution or display of the digitally generated electoral material containing a depiction of a simulated person occurred with the written consent of the real person depicted as the simulated person, or
the defendant—
took no part in determining the content of the digitally generated electoral material, and
could not reasonably be expected to have known that the digitally generated electoral material contravened subsection (1).
An apparent consent will not be an effective consent for this section if—
given by a person who is under the age of 17 years or has a cognitive impairment within the meaning of the Mental Health and Cognitive Impairment Forensic Provisions Act 2020, or
obtained from a person by duress or deception.
In this section—
depiction includes an audio visual, visual or audio depiction of a real person.
digitally generated electoral material—
means electoral material containing audio visual, visual or audio content that is generated substantially, or modified or altered significantly, by artificial intelligence, but
does not include—
a cartoon or animated drawing, or
electoral material that is of a kind, or generated in a way, prescribed by the regulations.
simulated person means a person depicted in digitally generated electoral material that—
purports to be a depiction of a particular real person, or
so closely resembles a depiction of a particular real person that a reasonable person would consider it likely to be a depiction of the real person.
The Minister must not recommend the making of a regulation under subsection (4), definition of digitally generated electoral material, paragraph (b)(ii) during the following periods—
the period—
commencing on 1 October in the year before a general election, and
ending on the election day for the general election,
the period—
commencing on the date of the issue of the writ for a by-election, and
ending on the day of the by-election.

heading.b: Digitally generated electoral material to include certain statements

block.txt: A person must not, during the regulated period, print, publish, distribute or publicly display digitally generated electoral material that depicts a digitally created person, event or place that a reasonable person would think is an actual person, event or place unless the material contains—
a statement that the material is digitally generated electoral material, and
the statement is—
for audio visual content—written and spoken, or
for visual content—written, or
for audio content—spoken.
Maximum penalty—
for an individual—20 penalty units or imprisonment for 6 months, or both, or
otherwise—100 penalty units.
The statement must be printed, published, distributed or publicly displayed or communicated, in a way, if any, prescribed by the regulations.
It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence against this section if the defendant establishes that the defendant—
took no part in determining the content of the digitally generated electoral material, and
could not reasonably be expected to have known that the digitally generated electoral material contravened subsection (1).
In this section—
digitally generated electoral material—see section 189A(4).
A person is not guilty of an offence for a breach of a provision of this Subdivision if it is established that—
the breach was not of a material nature, or
the breach was not intended, or was not likely, to mislead an elector in or in relation to the casting of his or her vote, or

the person was not aware that the act or omission concerned was a breach of the provision when it occurred and took all reasonable steps to remedy the breach when the person became aware that it was or may have been such a breach.
Nothing in this Subdivision prohibits—

the display, writing, drawing or depicting of a sign on or at the office or committee room of a candidate or political party indicating only that the office or room is the office or committee room of the candidate or party, and specifying the name of the candidate, or the names of the candidates, or the name of the party concerned, or

the projection by means of any cinema projector or other similar projector of any electoral matter on to any screen in any theatre or public hall the subject of a development consent in force under the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 in relation to its use as a place of public entertainment, or

the display, writing, drawing or depicting of any poster within a hall or room that is being or is about to be used for a meeting held by or on behalf of a candidate in connection with an election, or
the display of any poster on or at the office of a member.

heading.b: Additional offences applicable on early voting days
Display of posters on early voting days at early voting centres

block.txt: A person must not display, or cause to be displayed, any poster of any size—
within an early voting centre, or
within 6 metres of an entrance to an early voting centre, or
on the exterior of a building used as an early voting centre,
on any day on which early voting is conducted at the early voting centre.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of a corporation—50 penalty units, or
in any other case—10 penalty units.

heading.b: Canvassing on early voting days at early voting centres

block.txt: A person must not—
canvass for votes, or
solicit the vote of any elector, or
induce any elector not to vote for any particular candidate or group of candidates, or
induce any elector not to vote at the election,
within an early voting centre or within 6 metres of an entrance to an early voting centre on any day on which early voting is conducted at the early voting centre.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

heading.b: Amplified canvassing audible in early voting centre

block.txt: A person must not contravene this subsection. This subsection is contravened if, on any day on which early voting is conducted at an early voting centre, each of the following paragraphs apply—
the person engages in—
canvassing for votes, or
soliciting the vote of an elector, or
inducing an elector not to vote for a particular candidate or group of candidates, or
inducing an elector not to vote at the election,
the person engages, in any public or private place, in that activity any distance away from the early voting centre,
the person uses any of the following to engage in that activity—
a loud speaker,
a public address system,
an amplifier (whether fixed or mobile),
a broadcasting van,
a sound system,
radio equipment,
any other equipment or device for broadcasting,
that activity is audible within the early voting centre.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), a reference to canvassing for votes includes a reference to distributing electoral material, whether or not the material is registered in accordance with Subdivision 6.

The owner or occupier of premises that are being used as an early voting centre must not, without reasonable excuse, interfere with or remove or cause to be removed any poster that is exhibited or posted at those premises in compliance with the provisions of this Division.
Maximum penalty—10 penalty units.

heading.b: Additional offences applicable on election days
Distribution of electoral material on early voting days near early voting centre

block.txt: A person must not, within 100m of an early voting centre, distribute electoral material on a day on which early voting is conducted unless the material has been registered under Subdivision 6 for the election.
Maximum penalty—
for a corporation—100 penalty units, or
otherwise—20 penalty units or imprisonment for 6 months, or both.

For this section and without limiting its operation, material is taken to be distributed if it is left in a position and in circumstances that indicate that it is intended to be available for collection by members of the public.

This section does not apply to the handing out, distribution, sale or otherwise making available of a newspaper by or on behalf of a newsagent, newspaper seller or distributor if the handing out, distribution, sale or making available is in the course of the newsagent’s, newspaper seller’s or distributor’s employment or business.
Section 194 extends to this section.

In the application of this Subdivision to electoral material, electoral matter is, without limiting the definition of that term in section 4, taken to include any matter consisting of an express or implicit reference to or comment on—
an election, or
any council or any previous council, or
any councillor or previous councillor, or
the Government, the Opposition, a previous Government or a previous Opposition, of this or any other State or Territory or of the Commonwealth, or
a member or former member of the Parliament of this or any other State or Territory or of the Commonwealth, or
a political party, a branch or division of a political party or a candidate in an election, or
an issue submitted to, or otherwise before, the electors in connection with an election.
References in this Subdivision to election day include references to all days to which voting is adjourned.

heading.b: Distribution of electoral material on election days

block.txt: A person must not, in a public place, distribute any electoral material on election day unless the material has been registered under Subdivision 6 for the election.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of a corporation—100 penalty units, or
in any other case—20 penalty units or imprisonment for 6 months, or both.

For the purposes of this section and without limiting its operation, material is taken to be distributed if it is left in such a position and in such circumstances as to indicate that it is intended to be available for collection by members of the public who are in a public place.

This section does not apply to the handing out, distribution, sale or otherwise making available of a newspaper by or on behalf of a newsagent, newspaper seller or distributor if the handing out, distribution, sale or making available is in the course of the newsagent’s, newspaper seller’s or distributor’s employment or business.

heading.b: Display of posters on election days

block.txt: A person must not, on election day, display or cause to be displayed any poster of any size—
within a voting centre, or
within 6 metres of an entrance to a voting centre, or
on the exterior of a building used as a voting centre.
Maximum penalty—
in the case of a corporation—50 penalty units, or
in any other case—10 penalty units.

The owner or occupier of premises that are being used as a voting centre must not interfere with or remove or cause to be removed any poster that is exhibited or posted at those premises in compliance with the provisions of this Division.
Maximum penalty—10 penalty units.

heading.b: Canvassing in or near voting centre

block.txt: A person must not—
canvass for votes, or
solicit the vote of any elector, or
induce any elector not to vote for any particular candidate or group of candidates, or
induce any elector not to vote at the election,
on election day—
within a voting centre, or
within 6 metres of an entrance to a voting centre.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

heading.b: Amplified canvassing audible in or near voting centre

block.txt: A person must not contravene this subsection. This subsection is contravened if on election day each of the following paragraphs apply—
the person engages in—
canvassing for votes, or
soliciting the vote of an elector, or
inducing an elector not to vote for a particular candidate or group of candidates, or
inducing an elector not to vote at the election,
the person engages, in any public or private place, in that activity 6 metres or more from an entrance to a voting centre,
the person uses any of the following to engage in that activity—
a loud speaker,
a public address system,
an amplifier (whether fixed or mobile),
a broadcasting van,
a sound system,
radio equipment,
any other equipment or device for broadcasting,
that activity is audible—
within the voting centre, or
within 6 metres of an entrance to the voting centre.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

Without limiting the generality of subsection (1), a reference to canvassing for votes includes a reference to distributing electoral material, whether or not the material is registered in accordance with Subdivision 6.

heading.b: Application for registration of electoral material
Application for registration may be made

block.txt: An application may be made to the Electoral Commissioner for the registration of electoral material for a particular election or a particular district or districts.

heading.b: Applications by or on behalf of parties, groups or candidates

block.txt: An application may be made—
by the registered officer of a registered party—on behalf of the party, or
by the first candidate listed in a group of candidates—on behalf of the group, or
by a candidate—on his or her own behalf.

heading.b: Applications by or on behalf of others

block.txt: An application may be made—
by an officer or representative of an incorporated or unincorporated body (other than a registered party or a group) who is not a candidate—on behalf of the body, or
by an individual who is not a candidate—on his or her own behalf.
An application may only be made during the following periods (the application period)—
for an application for the registration of electoral material that is only to be supplied to voters at a declared facility—the period—
starting on nomination day, and
ending at 5pm on the Friday 8 days before election day, or
otherwise—the period—
starting on nomination day, and
ending at 5pm on the Thursday before election day.

heading.b: Draft or sample to be provided

block.txt: An application must contain a draft or sample of the electoral material.

heading.b: Alteration or replacement of draft or sample

block.txt: The Electoral Commissioner may allow the draft or sample to be altered or replaced during the application period before agreeing to registration.
An application under this section—
is to be in the approved form, and
is to be verified by the applicant in the approved manner (if any), and
For example, a written application may be verified by the signature of the applicant.
may be lodged with the Electoral Commissioner in a written or an electronic form.

heading.b: Application form to indicate if electoral material to be supplied to declared facility voters

block.txt: The approved form of application under this section must, if the electoral material to which it relates consists of or contains a how-to-vote card, allow the applicant to indicate whether or not that electoral material should be available for perusal by electors voting at a mobile voting centre at a declared facility.
The Electoral Commissioner must register the electoral material if satisfied that registration is not prohibited by this Subdivision.
However, the Electoral Commissioner may refuse to register the electoral material if the application for registration was not made in accordance with this Subdivision.

heading.b: When material must be refused registration

block.txt: The Electoral Commissioner must not register the electoral material if it appears to the Electoral Commissioner that—
the material contravenes Subdivision 2, or
the material is, or contains a section, in a language other than English and the application for registration was not accompanied by—
an accurate translation into English of the material or section, and
a declaration that the translation is accurate, or
the material does not include in visible, legible characters—
the name of an individual on whose instructions the material was produced, and
the address of that individual or, if the material was produced on behalf of a registered party, the name and address of the registered party as it appears on the Register of Parties, or
the material does not clearly identify the person, political party, organisation or group on whose behalf the material is to be distributed, or

in the case of an application for registration purporting to be made on behalf of an entity referred to in section 199 (2) or (3)—the application was not made by a person authorised by the relevant subsection to make the application, or

in the case of an application not purporting to be made on behalf of an entity referred to in section 199 (2) or (3) for the registration of material that contains voting directions as to how to vote for or in accordance with the recommendations of such an entity—the application was not made by a person authorised by the relevant subsection to make an application on behalf of the entity, or
in the case of an application for the registration of material that contains any representation or indication (whether express or implied) that any candidate—
is a member of, or
pursues or supports any or all of the objects or platform (whether with or without modification) of, or
is affiliated in some way (whether officially or unofficially) with,
a particular registered party or a group—the application was not made by or with the consent of the registered officer of the party or the first candidate listed in the group, or
the material contains words that are, or other matter that is, obscene or offensive.

heading.b: Inquiries as to authenticity of application or consent

block.txt: The Electoral Commissioner may make such inquiries as the Electoral Commissioner thinks fit to confirm the authenticity of—
an application, or
any consent referred to in subsection (3) (g).
The Electoral Commissioner must consider an application for the registration of electoral material within 24 hours of receiving the application if the application is received during the period—
starting at 5pm on the Friday 8 days before election day, and
ending at 5pm on the Thursday before election day.
Registration of the electoral material is effected by the issue of a certificate of registration in respect of a draft or sample of the electoral material.

heading.b: Details to be included in certificate

block.txt: The certificate of registration must specify the election and the district or districts for which the electoral material is registered.
A certificate of registration issued under this section is to be in the approved form.

heading.b: Registration may be conditional or unconditional

block.txt: Registration may be unconditional or subject to conditions specified in the certificate of registration.
A certificate signed by the Electoral Commissioner and certifying that specified material was or was not registered—
on a specified day or during a specified period, or
for a particular election, or
for a particular district or districts,
is admissible in proceedings for an offence under this Division and is prima facie evidence of the matters certified.

heading.b: Immaterial differences not to affect registration

block.txt: Electoral material is to be taken to be registered in accordance with this section even though the material contains some differences from the draft or sample in respect of which the certificate of registration was issued, so long as the material is substantially the same as the draft or sample.

heading.b: Registration not a defence for certain offences

block.txt: Registration of electoral material is not a defence to a prosecution for an offence under Subdivision 3 or 4.

heading.b: Copy of material and certificate to be available for public inspection

block.txt: The Electoral Commissioner must ensure that registered electoral material and the relevant certificate of registration are made available for public inspection on the Electoral Commission’s website—
for electoral material that is registered before 5pm on the Friday that is 8 days before election day—from the Monday preceding the election day until 6 pm on election day, or
for electoral material that is registered at or after 5pm on the Friday that is 8 days before election day—as soon as practicable after the material is registered until 6 pm on election day.

The Electoral Commissioner is not required to make copies of such electoral material or certificates of registration. However, a person inspecting any such material or certificates is entitled to use the person’s own device (such as a camera, mobile phone, video recorder or any other electronic device) to copy or record that material or those certificates and take away or transmit those copies.

heading.b: Revocation of registration or imposition of condition on registration

block.txt: If the Electoral Commissioner is satisfied that electoral material was erroneously registered, the Electoral Commissioner may—
revoke the registration of the material, or
attach a condition to the registration of the material, requiring the material to be altered in a specified way, whether by way of omitting matter or inserting matter or both, or otherwise.
The revocation or condition takes effect from the time the revocation or condition is communicated to the candidates concerned or their representatives, and accordingly—
electoral material whose registration has been revoked ceases to be registered from that time, and
electoral material to whose registration a condition has been attached is from that time taken to be registered only if the condition is complied with.

heading.b: Maintenance of safety and order at and near voting centres

block.txt: A police officer may remove a person from a voting centre or the immediate vicinity of a voting centre if the police officer has reasonable grounds to believe the person is committing, has committed or is attempting to commit an offence under this Act at that voting centre or in the immediate vicinity of that voting centre.
A police officer may remove or cause to be removed from a voting centre and from the immediate vicinity of the voting centre, any person—
who, having been given a lawful direction by or under the authority of the Electoral Commissioner or voting centre manager, fails to comply with that direction, or
who is obstructing the access or approaches to the voting centre, or
who is obstructing or unnecessarily delaying the proceedings at the voting centre, or
who is behaving in a disorderly manner or is causing a disturbance.
The Electoral Commissioner and every voting centre manager may give such directions as are necessary for the following purposes—
to protect persons at a place where voting is occurring under this Act from health and safety hazards caused by storm, fire, flood or another emergency,
to maintain order at an election or a place where voting is occurring under this Act.
A person must not, without lawful authority, contravene any such direction.
Maximum penalty (subsection (4)): 20 penalty units.

heading.b: Removal and confiscation of posters and other electoral material
Directions to remove posters and other electoral material

block.txt: The Electoral Commissioner or any voting centre manager, or any other election official authorised by the Electoral Commissioner or a voting centre manager may direct a person representing a party, group or candidate at a voting centre to remove, or cause to be removed—
any poster displayed at the voting centre by the party, group or candidate in contravention of Subdivision 3, 4 or 5, or
any electoral material that is apparently available for distribution at the voting centre by the party, group or candidate in contravention of Subdivision 5.
A person must not, without reasonable excuse, contravene any such direction.
Maximum penalty (subsection (2)): 20 penalty units.

The Electoral Commissioner or any voting centre manager, or any other election official authorised by the Electoral Commissioner or a voting centre manager, may remove and confiscate, or cause to be removed and confiscated—
any poster displayed in contravention of Subdivision 4 or 5, or
any electoral material that is apparently available for distribution in contravention of Subdivision 5.

heading.b: Confiscation by Electoral Commissioner and police

block.txt: The Electoral Commissioner or any police officer may remove and confiscate, or cause to be removed and confiscated—
any poster displayed in contravention of Subdivision 3, 4 or 5, or
any electoral material that is apparently available for distribution in contravention of Subdivision 5.
A police officer may use reasonable force for the purposes of this section. This section does not authorise any other person to use force.
Confiscated electoral material must be destroyed without undue delay, but destruction may be delayed if the material is or may reasonably be required for evidentiary purposes.
Nothing in this Division applies to the printing, publishing, distribution or display of official notices.
A person is not liable to be convicted of both an offence under Subdivision 3 and an offence under Subdivision 4 or 5 if the offences arose out of the same circumstances.

heading.b: Voting centre managers and election officials to consider guidelines before enforcing “6-metre” rules

block.txt: A voting centre manager or an election official must not exercise a function under this Division in relation to contravention of a 6-metre offence unless the manager or official has considered the guidelines, if any, issued under subsection (2).

The Electoral Commissioner may, from time to time, determine and issue guidelines, not inconsistent with this Act, about the exercise, by voting centre managers and election officials, of functions under this Division in relation to a contravention of a 6-metre offence.
In this section—
6-metre offence means an offence against the following—
section 191(b),
section 192(1), but not in relation to an activity within an early voting centre,
section 196(b),
section 198(1), but not in relation to an activity within a voting centre.

Section 11B of the Constitution Act 1902 provides that every person who is entitled to vote at a periodic Council election or the election of a Member of the Legislative Assembly must vote at the election and if the person does not do so, the person is liable to such penalty as may be provided by law.
An elector who fails to vote at an election is guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—1 penalty unit.
For the purposes of any proceedings for an offence against subsection (1), a person is taken to have voted if the person has—
been given a ballot paper by an election official and has placed that ballot paper in a ballot box (whether inside an envelope or not), or
posted or delivered a ballot paper in a postal voting envelope to the Electoral Commissioner (or caused it to be so posted or delivered), or
voted in any other manner permitted by this Act.

This provision is a machinery provision to make it clear that a prosecution under this section is subject to the principle of the secret ballot. A prosecutor should not and cannot prove in court that a person has marked their ballot paper in any particular manner.
It is not a defence to a prosecution under this section that the defendant did not know that the election was being conducted.
In this section, elector does not include—
an eligible overseas elector, or
an itinerant elector.
A person must not obstruct the access or approaches to a voting centre.
Maximum penalty—10 penalty units.

heading.b: Electoral bribery, treating and selling of votes

block.txt: A person must not, in order to influence or affect any person’s election conduct, give or confer, or promise or offer to give or confer, any property or any other benefit of any kind to the person or any other person.
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units or imprisonment for 3 years, or both.
A person must not—
ask for, receive or obtain, or
offer to ask for, receive or obtain, or
agree to ask for, receive or obtain,
any property or any other benefit of any kind, whether for the person or any other person, on an understanding that the person’s election conduct will be in any manner influenced or affected.
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units or imprisonment for 3 years, or both.
In this section, person’s election conduct means—
the way in which the person votes at an election, or
the person’s nomination as a candidate for an election, or
the person’s support of, or opposition to, a candidate or a political party at an election, or
the doing of any act or thing by the person the purpose of which is, or the effect of which is likely to be, to influence the preferences set out in the vote of an elector.
This section does not apply in relation to a declaration of public policy or a promise of public action.
An offence under this section is an indictable offence.
A person must not hinder or interfere with the free exercise, by any other person, of the person’s right to vote in an election under this Act.
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units or imprisonment for 3 years, or both.
A person must not, by violence or intimidation, influence the vote of a person at an election.
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units or imprisonment for 3 years, or both.
An offence under this section is an indictable offence.

heading.b: Photographing and recording of voting and scrutiny

block.txt: A person must not, in a voting centre or ballot counting place, take a photograph or make an audio or video recording.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

Subsection (1) does not apply to the taking of a photograph or the making of a an audio or video recording with the permission of the voting centre manager or person in charge of the ballot counting place.

heading.b: Photographing and recording election officials outside voting centres or ballot counting places

block.txt: A person must not, outside a voting centre or ballot counting place, take a photograph or make an audio or video recording of an election official or scrutineer if the photographing or recording is reasonably likely to cause the official or scrutineer to be intimidated or harassed.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A person must not publish or distribute a photograph or an audio or video recording made in the course of committing an offence against subsection (1).
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

heading.b: Ballot papers not to be removed from voting centre etc

block.txt: A person must not, without lawful authority—
remove a ballot paper from any voting centre, or
enter into a compartment of a voting centre while any person is in the compartment, or
remain in the compartment of a voting centre for a longer period than is necessary for the purpose of marking his or her ballot paper, or
obstruct or unnecessarily delay the proceedings at a voting centre.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units or imprisonment for 6 months, or both.
A person must not—
impersonate any elector for the purpose of voting at any election, or
vote more than once at any election.
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units or imprisonment for 3 years, or both.
An offence under this section is an indictable offence.

heading.b: Disorderly conduct at public political meetings

block.txt: A person must not, at any public meeting to which this section applies, act in a disorderly manner for the purpose of disrupting the meeting.
This section applies to any lawful public political meeting held in relation to any election between the date of the issue of the writ for the election and the date of the return of the writ.
Maximum penalty—5 penalty units.

A person must not intentionally break open a sealed package of ballot papers or other electoral material unless authorised to do so by the Electoral Commissioner or an election manager or required or authorised to do so by or under any legislation or direction of a court.
Maximum penalty—10 penalty units.

heading.b: Display, publish or distribute material falsely appearing to be made by Electoral Commission

block.txt: A person is guilty of an offence if—
the person displays, publishes or distributes material (or causes or permits material to be displayed, published or distributed), and
the person does so knowing that, or being reckless as to whether, the material falsely appears to have been authorised by the Electoral Commission or Electoral Commissioner.
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units or imprisonment for 2 years, or both.

heading.b: False or misleading declaration and statements

block.txt: A person must not make a declaration under this Part that the person knows is false or misleading in a material particular.
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units or imprisonment for 2 years, or both.

An elector must not in or in connection with an application under this Part, or for the purpose of or in connection with the casting of a vote by means of technology assisted voting, make any statement to an election official that the person knows is false or misleading in a material particular.
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units or imprisonment for 2 years, or both.
A person must not persuade or induce a person to make a declaration or statement of the kind referred to in subsection (1) or (2).
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units or imprisonment for 2 years, or both.

In this section, a reference to a statement to an election official includes a statement made by means of electronic communication sent to the Electoral Commissioner or the Electoral Commission’s website.

heading.b: Improperly signing or witnessing electoral papers

block.txt: A person must not do any of the following—
sign as witness a blank electoral paper,
sign as witness an electoral paper that has been wholly or partly filled up unless it has been signed by the signatory,
sign as witness an electoral paper unless the person has seen the signatory sign it,
write a name that is not his or her own name on an electoral paper as his or her own name,
sign an electoral paper with a signature that purports to be that of another person.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A person must not—
forge any electoral paper, or
utter any forged electoral paper, knowing it to be forged.
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units or imprisonment for 2 years, or both.
A person must not knowingly place in a ballot box—
any ballot paper that has not been lawfully issued to an elector, or
any other paper purporting to be a ballot paper other than a ballot paper lawfully issued to the elector.
Maximum penalty—200 penalty units or imprisonment for 2 years, or both.
A person, other than the Electoral Commissioner, must not distribute, or cause or permit to be distributed, an application to vote by post in an election under Division 10, unless—
the application is in the form approved by the Electoral Commission, and
the form states that the application must be submitted directly to the Electoral Commissioner, and
no additional information or matter appears on the application.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
It is not an offence under subsection (1) for a person to make available at a post office an application to vote by post provided by the Electoral Commissioner.
A person must not solicit another person to return or submit the other person’s application to vote by post to anyone other than the Electoral Commissioner.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

A person, other than the Electoral Commissioner, must not, in connection with the distribution or collection of another person’s application to vote by post, collect personal information about the other person without the other person’s written consent.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

heading.b: Death of candidate during election period
Death of candidate before close of nominations

block.txt: If a candidate for an election dies, after being nominated and before 12 noon on the nomination day for the election, the day named as the nomination day for that election is taken to be the day following the named nomination day.

heading.b: Death of candidate after close of nominations but before 6 pm on election day

block.txt: If after 12 noon on the nomination day and before 6 pm on the election day for an election for any district, any candidate dies—
the election is taken to have failed, and
a new writ is to be issued for an election for the district.

If, after 12 noon on the nomination day and before the election day of a periodic Council election, any candidate dies and there are not more than 21 candidates remaining, the Electoral Commissioner is to publicly declare the remaining candidates to be duly elected and publicly advertise the declaration and return the writ endorsed according to that declaration.
If, after 12 noon on the nomination day and before the election day of a periodic Council election, any candidate dies and there are more than 21 candidates remaining—
the election is not taken to have failed, and
if the deceased candidate is elected, a vacancy is taken to occur.

heading.b: Death of candidate after 6 pm on election day

block.txt: If after 6 pm on election day for any election, but before the election has been declared, a candidate in the election dies—
the election is not taken to have failed, and
if the deceased candidate is elected, a vacancy is taken to occur.

heading.b: Election not to be questioned for omission etc of a formal nature

block.txt: An election for a district is not void because of any delay in the return of the writ.

An election for a district or a periodic Council election is not void because of a vacancy in the office of Electoral Commissioner at the time of the issue of the writ or any delay in the return of the writ.
Where any accidental or unavoidable impediment, misfeasance or omission has happened, the Governor—
may by proclamation declare any or all of the proceedings at or for any election valid as to and notwithstanding the impediment, misfeasance, or omission.
Every such proclamation must state specifically the nature of the impediment, misfeasance or omission concerned and must be published in the Gazette.
After an election, the Electoral Commissioner must ensure that the following information is publicly available—
the number of first preference votes given for each candidate,
in relation to a periodic Council election—the number of first preference votes given for each group,
the details of distribution of preference votes.
After an election, the Electoral Commissioner must ensure that—
each registered party that so requests, and
each member of Parliament who is not a member of a registered party and who makes a request in respect of the member’s district,

is provided with election information containing the names and the addresses of electors who voted (other than silent electors and itinerant electors), whether they voted personally, by post or by another method authorised under this Act and, if they voted at a voting centre for the district for which the electors were enrolled, the location of that voting centre.
Election information provided under subsection (2) must only be used in connection with an election.
A person must not use, or cause or permit the use of, election information provided under this section for any purpose other than in connection with an election.
Maximum penalty—1,000 penalty units.

The Electoral Commissioner may, before providing information under subsection (2), require the registered party or member of Parliament give the Electoral Commissioner an undertaking that the party or member’s systems and procedures will be adequate to preserve the security of that information.
A person must not, without reasonable excuse, refuse or fail to comply with an undertaking given under subsection (5).
Maximum penalty—1,000 penalty units.
The regulations may deal with the making of undertakings under this section.
Subsection (9) applies if the Electoral Commissioner believes it necessary to ensure either of the following is not ascertainable—
the way an elector voted at an election,
health information, within the meaning of the Health Records and Information Privacy Act 2002, about an elector.
Despite subsection (2), the Electoral Commissioner may—
refuse to provide the requested election information, or
give the election information in a form or format that the Electoral Commissioner believes ensures the information is not ascertainable.
Division 7 of Part 5 (Inspection of authorised rolls and lists of enrolled persons and provision of enrolment information) contains provisions regarding access to certain enrolment information.

heading.b: Signatures and marks on electoral papers and ballot papers

block.txt: An electoral paper that is required to be signed by a person is to be signed by that person with his or her personal signature.

If a person who is unable to sign his or her name in writing makes his or her mark as his or her signature on an electoral paper, the mark is taken to be his or her personal signature, if it is identifiable as the person’s mark and is made in the presence of a witness who signs the electoral paper as a witness.

If a person is unable to mark a ballot paper or sign and complete an electoral paper without assistance or is under a religious obligation not to mark a ballot paper or sign and complete an electoral paper with his or her own hand, the person may appoint another person to mark the ballot paper or sign and complete the electoral paper on that person’s behalf.
The Supreme Court is the Court of Disputed Returns for the purposes of this Act.
The jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, sitting as the Court of Disputed Returns, may be exercised by a single Judge.
The Court of Disputed Returns has the following powers in relation to a petition—
the power to adjourn,
the power to compel the attendance of witnesses and the production of documents,

the power to grant to any party to a petition leave to inspect, in the presence of a member of staff of the Electoral Commission, the authorised rolls and other documents (except ballot papers) used at or in connection with any election and to take, in the presence of the staff member, copies or extracts of those rolls and documents,
the power to order the staff of the Electoral Commission to print any technology assisted voting image files of ballot papers of votes cast in an election to enable a further count to be made,
the power to examine witnesses on oath,
the power to declare that any person who was returned as elected was not duly elected,
the power to declare any candidate duly elected who was not returned as elected,
the power to declare any election absolutely void,
the power to dismiss or uphold the petition in whole or in part,
the power to award costs,
the power to punish any contempt of its authority by fine or imprisonment,
such other powers as are conferred or imposed on the Court.
The Court may exercise all or any of its powers under this section on such grounds as the Court in its discretion thinks just and sufficient.
Without limiting the powers conferred by this section, the following powers of the Court may be exercised on the ground that illegal practices were committed in connection with the election—
to declare that any person who was returned as elected was not duly elected,
to declare an election absolutely void.

heading.b: Court to sit as open court

block.txt: The Court of Disputed Returns is to sit as an open court.

The Court of Disputed Returns is to be guided by the substantial merits and good conscience of each case without regard to legal forms or technicalities or whether the evidence before it is in accordance with the law of evidence or not.
All decisions of the Court of Disputed Returns are final and conclusive and without appeal and are not to be questioned in any way.
No appeal lies to the Court of Appeal from any decision of the Court.
Subsection (2) does not limit the generality of subsection (1).

If the Court of Disputed Returns declares that a person declared elected was not elected, the person ceases to be a member of the Assembly or Council, as the case requires, from the date determined by the Court.
If the Court declares that a person not declared elected was elected, the person may take his or her seat in the Assembly or Council, as the case requires, from the date determined by the Court.
If the Court declares that an election is void, a new election must be held.

If a new election is to be held under subsection (3) to return a member of the Assembly, the Speaker must issue the writ for the election or, if there is no Speaker by reason of illness or due to some other cause the Speaker is unable to issue the writ, the Governor may issue the writ.

Section 31A of the Constitution Act 1902 provides that, when the Speaker is unavailable, the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly is to act in his or her place and has and may exercise and perform all the powers, authorities, duties and functions of the Speaker, including those functions conferred under this section.
If a new periodic Council election is to be held under subsection (3), the Governor may issue the writ for that election.

heading.b: Power to make Rules of Court

block.txt: Rules not inconsistent with this Act may be made under the Supreme Court Act 1970 for carrying this Part into effect, and in particular for regulating the practice and procedure of the Court of Disputed Returns and the forms to be used.
Subsection (1) does not limit the rule-making powers conferred by the Supreme Court Act 1970.

Despite the Supreme Court Act 1970, any provision of that Act and any provision of any rule made by or pursuant to that Act which is inconsistent with this Act is, to the extent of such inconsistency and while such inconsistency continues to exist, not to apply to or in respect of any proceedings under this Part.
The Governor may make regulations fixing or otherwise relating to fees to be paid by parties in respect of the business of the Court of Disputed Returns.

This Division does not apply to or in respect of an election referred to in section 22D of the Constitution Act 1902 (Filling of casual vacancies in seats of Members of Legislative Council by joint sitting of both Houses).
See Division 4 of this Part in relation to elections to fill casual vacancies in seats of members of Legislative Council.

heading.b: Method of disputing elections or returns

block.txt: The validity of any election or return may be disputed only by a petition to the Court of Disputed Returns.
A petition disputing an election or return in this Part (a petition) must—
set out—
the facts relied on to invalidate the election or return, and
the relief claimed by the petitioner and the order sought from the Court, and
be signed by—
a candidate at the election in dispute, or
a person who was qualified to vote at the election, or
the Electoral Commissioner, and
be attested by 2 witnesses whose occupations and addresses are stated, and
be filed with the Prothonotary of the Supreme Court within 40 days of the return of the writ.
At the time of filing the petition the petitioner must deposit with the Prothonotary the sum of $250 as security for costs.
The Court of Disputed Returns must not deal with any proceedings on the petition unless the requirements of this section are complied with.

heading.b: Right of Electoral Commissioner to be represented

block.txt: The Electoral Commissioner may, by leave of the Court of Disputed Returns—
enter an appearance in any proceedings in which the validity of any election or return is disputed, and
be represented and heard in those proceedings.
If leave to appear is granted by the Court, the Electoral Commissioner is taken to be a party respondent to the petition.
The Court of Disputed Returns—
is to inquire whether or not the petition has been properly filed, and
may inquire into the identity of persons who voted, whether they were entitled to do so and whether their votes were improperly admitted or rejected, and
must not inquire into the correctness of any authorised roll.

If the Court of Disputed Returns finds that a successful candidate has committed or has attempted to commit an offence under section 209 (Electoral bribery, treating and selling of votes) or 210 (Interference with right to vote), his or her election is to be declared void.
A finding by the Court of Disputed Returns does not bar or prejudice any prosecution for any illegal practice.
The Court of Disputed Returns is not to declare that any person returned as elected was not duly elected or declare any election void—
on the ground of any illegal practice committed by any person (other than the candidate) and without the candidate’s knowledge or authority, or
on the ground of any illegal practice other than a contravention or attempted contravention of section 209 (Electoral bribery, treating and selling of votes) or 210 (Interference with right to vote),

unless the Court is satisfied that the result of the election was likely to be affected and that it is just that the candidate should be declared not to be duly elected or that the election should be declared void.

heading.b: Court to report cases of illegal practices

block.txt: If the Court of Disputed Returns finds that any person has committed an illegal practice, the Prothonotary is, as soon as is reasonably practicable, to report the finding to the Governor.

heading.b: Immaterial errors not to void election

block.txt: An election is not to be voided on account of any delay in the declaration of nominations, voting or the return of the writ or on account of the absence or error of, or omission by, any officer which did not affect the result of the election.

However, if any elector was, on account of the absence or error of, or omission by, any officer, prevented from voting in any election, the Court of Disputed Returns is not, for the purpose of determining whether the absence or error of, or omission by, the officer did or did not affect the result of the election, to admit any evidence of the way in which the elector intended to vote at the election.

heading.b: Evidence that person not permitted to vote

block.txt: On the trial of any petition the Court of Disputed Returns is not to admit the evidence of any witness that he or she was not permitted to vote at any election unless the witness satisfies the Court—
that he or she claimed to vote at the election pursuant to that provision of this Act under which he or she was entitled or might be permitted to vote, and
that he or she complied with the requirements of this Act and the regulations relating to voting by electors in so far as he or she was permitted so to do.

heading.b: Copies of petition and order of court to be sent to Clerk of Assembly or Council

block.txt: The Prothonotary is, as soon as is reasonably practicable after the filing of a petition disputing an election for or the return of a member of the Assembly, to forward to the Clerk of the Assembly a copy of the petition and, after the trial of the petition, is, as soon as is reasonably practicable, to forward to that Clerk a copy of the order of the Court.

The Prothonotary is, as soon as is reasonably practicable after the filing of a petition disputing a periodic Council election or the return of a member of the Council, to forward to the Clerk of the Council a copy of the petition and, after the trial of the petition, is, as soon as is reasonably practicable, to forward to that Clerk a copy of the order of the Court.
A party to the petition is not, except by consent of all parties or by leave of the Court of Disputed Returns, to be represented by an Australian legal practitioner.
No more than one Australian legal practitioner is to appear on behalf of any party.
The Court of Disputed Returns may—
award costs against an unsuccessful party to the petition, and
recommend, in its discretion, that costs be paid by the Crown.
The Court must not recommend that the costs of an unsuccessful party to a petition be paid by the Crown except in exceptional circumstances.
If costs are awarded to any party against the petitioner, the deposit is to be applied in payment of the sum ordered, but otherwise the deposit is to be repaid to the petitioner.

All other costs awarded by the Court of Disputed Returns, including any balance above the deposit payable by the petitioner, are recoverable as if the order of the Court were a judgment of the Supreme Court, and such order may be entered as a judgment of the Supreme Court and enforced accordingly.

heading.b: Reference of question as to qualification or vacancy

block.txt: The Assembly may by resolution refer to the Court of Disputed Returns any question respecting—
the qualification of a member to be or continue as a member of the Assembly, or
a vacancy in the Assembly.
The Council may by resolution refer to the Court of Disputed Returns any question respecting—
the qualification of a member to be or continue as a member of the Council, or
a vacancy in the Council.
The Court of Disputed Returns has jurisdiction to hear and determine such a question.

heading.b: Speaker or President to state case

block.txt: If any question is referred to the Court of Disputed Returns under this Division, the Speaker or President is to provide to the Court—
a statement of the question that the Court is to hear and determine, and
any proceedings, papers, reports or documents relating to the question in the possession of the Assembly or Council.
The Court of Disputed Returns may—
allow any person, who in the opinion of the Court is interested in the determination of any question referred to it under this Division, to be heard on the hearing of the reference, or
direct notice of the reference to be served on any person,
and any person so allowed to be heard or so directed to be served is taken to be a party to the reference.
The powers of the Court of Disputed Returns, on the hearing of any reference under this Division, include the following—
the powers conferred on the Court by section 225 so far as they are applicable,
the power to declare that any person was not qualified to be a member of the Assembly or the Council,
the power to declare that any person was not capable of sitting as a member of the Assembly or the Council,
the power to declare that there is a vacancy in the Assembly or the Council.

Despite subsection (1) (a), the Court does not, in relation to a reference of a question regarding the qualification of a member to be or continue as a member of the Council or a vacancy in the Council, have the following powers—
the power to declare any candidate duly elected who was not returned as elected,
the power to declare any election absolutely void.

heading.b: Order to be sent to House affected

block.txt: After the hearing and determination of any reference under this Division the Prothonotary is, as soon as is reasonably practicable, to forward to the Clerk of the Assembly or the Clerk of the Council, as the case requires, a copy of the order or declaration of the Court of Disputed Returns.

The provisions of sections 242 (Australian legal practitioner), 243 (Costs) and 245 (Other costs) apply, so far as applicable, to proceedings on a reference to the Court of Disputed Returns under this Division.

heading.b: Disputed election to fill casual vacancies in Legislative Council

block.txt: This Division applies only to and in respect of an election referred to in section 22D of the Constitution Act 1902.

heading.b: Application of Divisions 1 and 2 to elections to fill casual vacancies in Legislative Council

block.txt: Divisions 1 and 2 (other than sections 232, 235–238, 240 and 241) apply to and in respect of an election to which this Division applies in the same way as they apply to and in respect of an election to which those Divisions apply.
However, the application of Divisions 1 and 2 is subject to the following modifications—
the Court of Disputed Returns does not, in relation to any such election, have the following powers—
the power to declare any candidate duly elected who was not returned as elected,
the power to declare any election absolutely void,
section 229 is taken to read as follows—
If a person is declared not to be elected, the person ceases to be a member of the Council.
section 234 (1) (b) is taken to read as follows—
be signed by an enrolled person of or above the age of 18 years, and
section 239 is taken to read as follows—

heading.b: Immaterial errors do not void election

block.txt: An election is not to be voided on account of any failure to comply with any provision of any Act relating to the conduct of the election if the failure did not affect the result of the election.
Proceedings for an offence under this Act or the regulations may be dealt with—
summarily before the Local Court, or
summarily before the Supreme Court in its summary jurisdiction.

If proceedings are brought in the Local Court, the maximum monetary penalty that the Local Court may impose for the offence is 200 penalty units, despite any higher maximum monetary penalty provided in respect of the offence.
Proceedings in respect of an offence against this Act or the regulations may be commenced only within 3 years after the offence was committed.

Section 10 (2) (b) of this Act (which confers a function of instituting proceedings for certain offences on the Electoral Commission) operates to extend and not limit the persons who may institute proceedings for those offences.
Proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations may only be commenced with the consent of the Electoral Commission.
Subsection (1) does not apply to proceedings for an offence that is declared by this Act to be an indictable offence.

heading.b: Proof of certain matters not required

block.txt: In any legal proceedings, proof is not required (until prima facie evidence is given to the contrary) of the following—
the constitution of the Electoral Commission,
any resolution of the Electoral Commission,
the appointment of or holding of office by the Electoral Commissioner or any other member of the Electoral Commission,
the presence or nature of a quorum at any meeting of the Electoral Commission.

A certificate signed by the Electoral Commissioner certifying that a specified person was or was not enrolled in respect of a specified address at a specified time or during a specified period is admissible in any proceedings and is prima facie evidence of the matter certified.

heading.b: Prosecution of parties that are unincorporated associations

block.txt: Proceedings for an offence under this Act alleged to have been committed by a party that is an unincorporated association (whether the subject of the offence provision is described as a party or a person) may be brought against the party in its own name (and not in the name of any of its members), and, for the purposes of those proceedings, any rules of court relating to the service of documents, are taken to have effect as if the party were a corporation.

A fine imposed on a party that is an unincorporated association for an offence under this Act is payable out of the property of the party and is not payable out of the property of the members or officers of the party unless the property is held for or on behalf of the party.

The Criminal Procedure Act 1986 has effect in a case in which a party that is an unincorporated association is charged with an offence under this Act in the same manner as it has effect in the case of a corporation charged with such an offence.

For the purpose of enforcing compliance with this Act, the Electoral Commission may exercise any investigative or other functions the Electoral Commission has under the Electoral Funding Act 2018 for the purpose of enforcing compliance with that Act.
Accordingly, a reference in Part 9 of that Act to “this Act” is taken to be a reference to this Act.

heading.b: Penalty notice for offence of failing to vote
Penalty notices for offence of failing to vote

block.txt: The Electoral Commissioner must, after every election, prepare a list of the names of the electors who were entitled to vote at the election and did not vote.
If an elector is indicated on a list as not having voted at the election, the Electoral Commissioner, within 3 months after the election day concerned, must issue a penalty notice to the elector.
A penalty notice is a notice to the effect that, if the elector does not wish to have the failure to vote dealt with by a court, the person may, within the time specified in the notice—
give the Electoral Commissioner a sufficient reason for the failure, or
pay to the Electoral Commissioner a penalty, specified in the notice, not exceeding $55.

An elector must not, in response to a penalty notice issued under this section, make a statement that gives a reason for the failure of an elector to vote that the elector knows to be false or misleading in a material particular.
Maximum penalty—1 penalty unit.
The Fines Act 1996 applies to a penalty notice issued under this section.

The Fines Act 1996 provides that, if a person issued with a penalty notice does not wish to have the matter determined by a court, the person may pay the amount specified in the notice and is not liable to any further proceedings for the alleged offence.
The Electoral Commissioner is not required to issue a penalty notice to an elector if it appears to the Commissioner that the elector has a sufficient reason for the failure to vote.
If, in response to a penalty notice and within the time specified for the response—
the Electoral Commissioner is given a sufficient reason for the failure to vote, or
the penalty specified in the notice is paid to the Electoral Commissioner,
no person is liable to any further proceedings for the alleged offence.

If, in response to a penalty notice, the Electoral Commissioner is given a reason for the failure to vote, but the reason is not a sufficient reason, the Electoral Commissioner is to include a statement to that effect in any penalty reminder notice issued under the Fines Act 1996.
For the purposes of this section, it is a sufficient reason for the failure of an elector to vote at an election if the Electoral Commissioner is satisfied that the elector—
was absent from New South Wales on election day, or
was ineligible to vote at the election, or
had an honest belief that abstention from voting was part of his or her religious duty, or
had a lack of mental capacity (as certified by a registered medical practitioner), or
was unable, for any reason acceptable to the Electoral Commissioner, to vote at the election.
For the avoidance of doubt, it is not a sufficient reason for the failure of an elector to vote at an election that the elector did not know that an election was being conducted.
In this section, a reference to the time specified, in relation to a response to a penalty notice is a reference to—
the time for response specified in the notice, or
if the Electoral Commissioner extends that time (whether before or after its expiration)—the extended time.

heading.b: Notation on list of non-voters of response to penalty notice

block.txt: The Electoral Commissioner is to note on the list prepared under section 259, in relation to each elector to whom a penalty notice is issued—
whether or not there has been a response to the notice, and
if there has been a response—whether or not a sufficient reason has been given or the penalty paid.
An entry on the list prepared under section 259 to the effect—
that a penalty notice was issued to an elector—is evidence of the issue of the notice, or
that there was no response to a penalty notice issued to an elector—is evidence that there was no such response within the time specified under section 259, or
that a reason for an elector’s failure to vote was given in response to a penalty notice but was insufficient—is evidence that the reason given was not a sufficient reason under section 259.
A list prepared under section 259 containing the name of an elector is evidence that the elector did not vote at the election.

Subsections (1) and (2) apply in relation to a copy of, or an extract from, the list prepared under section 259, certified by the Electoral Commissioner to be a true copy or extract, in the same way as those provisions apply in relation to the list prepared under section 259.

heading.b: Opening sealed packages containing rolls used at election

block.txt: For the purposes of this Act, the Electoral Commissioner at any election—
may open and if necessary break the seal of any package containing the authorised rolls used at the election, and examine those rolls for the purpose of preparing the list under section 259, and
at the conclusion of the examination must replace those rolls in the packages from which they were taken, and re-seal them, and comply with the provisions of section 175, as the case requires.
An authorised officer may issue a penalty notice to a person if it appears to the officer that the person has committed a penalty notice offence.

A penalty notice offence is an offence against this Act (other than an offence against section 207 (Offence of failing to vote)) or the regulations that is prescribed by the regulations as a penalty notice offence.
The Fines Act 1996 applies to a penalty notice issued under this section.

The Fines Act 1996 provides that, if a person issued with a penalty notice does not wish to have the matter determined by a court, the person may pay the amount specified in the notice and is not liable to any further proceedings for the alleged offence.

The amount payable under a penalty notice issued under this section is the amount prescribed for the alleged offence by the regulations (not exceeding the maximum amount of penalty that could be imposed for the offence by a court).
This section does not limit the operation of any other provision of, or made under, this or any other Act relating to proceedings that may be taken in respect of offences.
In this section, authorised officer means an inspector within the meaning of the Electoral Funding Act 2018.

heading.b: Matters relating to conduct of elections
Destruction of ballot papers and other documents

block.txt: Any provision of this Act that provides for the destruction of ballot papers or other documents has effect despite section 21 of the State Records Act 1998.

The Governor may, by order addressed to the Treasurer, authorise and direct that all such moneys as are from time to time required for paying any expenses lawfully incurred under and in the execution of the provisions of this Act be paid out of the Consolidated Fund, and those expenses are accordingly appropriated to the extent necessary.

heading.b: Provision as to Sunday and public holidays

block.txt: If the last day of a period of time prescribed or allowed by this Act for the doing of any thing falls—
on a Sunday, or
on a day that is a public holiday or bank holiday in the place in which the thing is to be or may be done,
the thing may be done on the first day following that is not a Sunday, or a public holiday or bank holiday in that place, as the case requires.

The Governor may make regulations, not inconsistent with this Act, for or with respect to any matter that by this Act is required or permitted to be prescribed or that is necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
If—
alteration of a form in the Schedules to this Act is necessary, or
